name: Yingkong (硬控)
blurb: Gaming slang for "hard control": something so captivating you can't look away
title: Yingkong (硬控) Meaning: Chinese Slang for "Hard Control"
description: Yingkong (硬控, "hard control") began as a gaming term for stun skills. Online, "X硬控我N秒" means something was so captivating you froze and stared.
answer: Yingkong (硬控, "hard control") started as a term in MOBA and other games for crowd-control skills such as knock-ups, petrify or freeze that leave an opponent's character unable to move for a while. In 2024 Chinese internet users began applying it to themselves: "this video hard-controlled me for 10 seconds" means it was so captivating that you froze and could not look away. It was named one of the top ten Chinese buzzwords of 2024 by the language magazine 《咬文嚼字》 (Yaowen Jiaozi).

body: 控 means control. Games split control effects into soft ones, such as slows or silences, where you can still act a little, and hard ones, such as knock-ups, stuns and freezes, where you cannot act at all. That second kind is 硬控.

Online, the target is now the viewer. A gorgeous clip, a hypnotic dance or a cute animal that makes you stop and replay it has "hard-controlled" you. A duration is often added, as in 硬控我30秒 (hard-controlled me for 30 seconds): the longer, the stronger the pull.

ul: In comments: "这个转圈硬控我十秒。" (That spin held me for ten seconds.)
On cute animals: "被这只啃竹笋的小熊猫硬控了。" (This red panda eating bamboo shoots has me frozen.)
On a show: "这部剧硬控了我一整个周末。" (This series held me hostage all weekend.)
Ironically: "开会被老板硬控两小时。" (Hard-controlled by my boss in a two-hour meeting.)

faq.a: "It hard-controlled me for a few seconds": something was so captivating that you stopped and stared. A bigger number means a stronger pull.

faq.q: What is the difference between hard control and soft control?
faq.a: In games, soft control (slows, silences) still lets you act partly, while hard control (stuns, knock-ups, freezes) stops you completely. The slang borrows the "can't move at all" sense.

faq.q: Was 硬控 a word of the year?
faq.a: Yes. On 2 December 2024, the editors of 《咬文嚼字》 ranked it No. 5 on their top ten buzzwords of 2024.
